quote.translation: When Plato, on the other hand, criticises the atomists by saying that "according to what they say, it seems that nature (φύσις) and chance (τύχη) made the greatest and most beautiful things, and art made the lesser" (Platon, Leges, X, 889), or "not through mind, nor through any god, nor through art, but through nature (φύσις) and chance (τύχη)" (Ib.), the chance he means is properly understood as teleological contingency in heterogeneous combination with the causal necessity called nature.
